quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: How do you know where traffic is behind you?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror often.
Turn and look out your back window.
Keep other vehicles out of your blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your rearview mirror often.
questions.explanation: Check your rearview mirror often to see where traffic is behind you.

questions.question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while driving, you should:

options.text: Pump the brake pedal hard several times.
Slow down gradually without braking.
Press the brake pedal down as hard as you can.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down gradually without braking.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly. Take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Let the car slow down on its own. Use the brakes gently only if needed. Pull off the road when it is safe.

questions.question: When you enter traffic from a parked spot at the curb, you should:

options.text: Drive slower than other traffic for 200 feet.
Wait for a big enough gap to reach the speed of traffic.
Wait for two vehicles to pass, then drive into the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for a big enough gap to reach the speed of traffic.
questions.explanation: When merging into city or highway traffic, wait for a gap large enough for your vehicle to reach the speed of other traffic.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
No U-turns.
No left turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers that right turns are not allowed at this location.

questions.question: If you see a single broken white line on a highway, you:

options.text: Cannot cross the line to pass.
May cross the line to pass and change lanes.
May only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: May cross the line to pass and change lanes.
questions.explanation: White dashed lines separate traffic going the same direction. You can cross a dashed white line to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:

options.text: Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.
The truck to stop.
Other drivers when they slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: The truck to stop.
questions.explanation: Trucks need more distance to stop than cars at the same speed. Do not pull in front of a truck and then slow down.

questions.question: Which of these slows down traffic?

options.text: Slowing down to look at a crash.
Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.
Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slowing down to look at a crash.
questions.explanation: Slowing down to look at crashes causes traffic congestion and should be avoided.

questions.question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Continue ahead. You have the right-of-way.
Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
Drive around the pedestrians to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait for the pedestrians to cross.
questions.explanation: Drivers must let pedestrians in crosswalks cross first. Wait until the crosswalk is clear before driving.

questions.question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent:

options.text: Has no effect on your driving.
Does not put other drivers at risk.
Doubles your chances of having an accident.

questions.correctAnswerText: Doubles your chances of having an accident.
questions.explanation: Each 0.02 percent increase in blood alcohol nearly doubles the risk of a fatal crash.

questions.question: On roadways, bicycles are considered:

options.text: Hazards.
Vehicles.
Dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: Vehicles.
questions.explanation: Bicycles are vehicles on roadways. Bicyclists and drivers must follow the same traffic rules.

questions.question: When driving near a large commercial vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Follow closely behind it to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.
Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
Drive on its right side when going around curves and hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not drive beside it for long periods of time.
questions.explanation: Large commercial vehicles have large blind spots on both sides. You should not drive beside them for long periods of time.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road ends ahead.
The road splits. You must turn right or left.
A four-way intersection is coming.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road splits. You must turn right or left.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign warns that the road splits ahead and you must choose to go either right or left.

questions.question: What type of drug is alcohol?

options.text: A stimulant.
A depressant.
Neither of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: A depressant.
questions.explanation: Alcohol is a depressant. It slows nerve impulses and body functions. It reduces inhibitions and hurts your ability to concentrate and stay alert.

questions.question: If arrested for a first DUI and you refuse a breath test, how long will your license be suspended?

options.text: At least 14 days.
At least 45 days.
At least 21 days.

questions.correctAnswerText: At least 45 days.
questions.explanation: If you refuse a breath test, your license will be suspended for at least 45 days. You will also need to install an ignition interlock device to get your license back.

questions.question: If you see a pedestrian with a guide dog or white cane, what should you do?

options.text: The pedestrian must yield to you.
You must yield to the pedestrian.
Honk your horn to warn them.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must yield to the pedestrian.
questions.explanation: A guide dog or white cane shows that a person is blind or partially blind. You must yield the right-of-way to these pedestrians.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a gap in highway traffic?

options.text: Watch only the vehicles behind the gap.
Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
Speed up and make other vehicles move.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check behind you, then watch the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes or entering traffic, check for vehicles beside and behind your car. Make sure the lane is clear before you move.

questions.question: What should you do when driving in a construction zone?

options.text: Drive slightly faster.
Be prepared for unexpected conditions.
Construction workers will move out of your way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be prepared for unexpected conditions.
questions.explanation: Construction zones have unexpected conditions. Drive with extra care to protect yourself, other drivers, and construction workers.

questions.question: Should you always drive slower than other traffic?

options.text: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.
Yes, it is always safer than driving faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, driving too slowly can block traffic.
questions.explanation: Drive slowly in heavy traffic or bad weather. But if you drive too slowly and block traffic, you can be cited.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Driving too slowly is safe.
Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
Speed does not affect safety.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.
questions.explanation: Driving too slowly can be dangerous. Other drivers may become frustrated and make unsafe moves to pass you. The safest approach is to drive with the flow of traffic within the speed limit.

questions.question: What is the purpose of rumble strips?

options.text: They warn drivers about tire problems.
They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.
They make noise and vibrations to alert drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: They make noise and vibrations to alert drowsy drivers that they are leaving the road.
questions.explanation: Rumble strips create noise and vibrations to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the road or approaching a stop sign or traffic signal.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line down the center of a road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.
Passing is allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from either direction.
questions.explanation: Broken yellow lines mean any driver can pass when it is safe. Check for oncoming traffic before you pass.

questions.question: What is the minimum gap you need to safely enter highway traffic?

options.text: A two-second gap.
A three-second gap.
A four-second gap.

questions.correctAnswerText: A four-second gap.
questions.explanation: You need a four-second opening to merge safely. This gives you and the driver behind you each a two-second following distance.

questions.question: What should you do before passing on a two-lane road?

options.text: Sound your horn as you pass.
Flash your headlights as you pass.
Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the distance to any oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: Oncoming vehicles may look slower than they really are. Always make sure you have enough space to pass safely. If you are unsure about an oncoming vehicle's speed, wait until it passes before you pass.

questions.question: What sign is this?

options.text: Yield sign.
School crossing sign.
Stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield sign.
questions.explanation: A downward-pointing triangle is always a yield sign. Slow down or stop if needed when you see this sign.

questions.question: You see a green light, but traffic is blocking the intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Partially enter to claim your right-of-way.
Do not enter until you can drive all the way across.
Enter and wait for traffic to clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not enter until you can drive all the way across.
questions.explanation: Never enter an intersection unless you can completely cross it before the light turns red. Blocking an intersection can result in a citation.
